reference: There is no GNU/POSIX command implementing this Bash builtin API, so runnable cases are contracts rather than GNU parity. Expected code points and byte lengths are independently derived from the UTF-8 encodings of the stated Unicode scalars; cluster expectations follow the documented decode-one-scalar plus combining-mark, variation-selector, and ZWJ-linked behavior. Bash type/help checks use Bash metadata builtins.
coverage: ASCII and 2-, 3-, and 4-byte UTF-8 scalar decoding, including U+10FFFF
Combining marks, variation selectors, emoji modifiers, and repeated ZWJ joins
Malformed hex and malformed, truncated, surrogate, and out-of-range UTF-8 rejection
read from standard input and an explicitly selected file descriptor
Empty input failure and preservation of the next scalar across successive reads
Owned pipe EOF, Unicode clusters and multibyte scalar lookahead.
Independent descriptor switches, duplicate aliases, ordinary FD reuse, and seek-back on regular files.
exclusions: No matching external GNU/POSIX wget_wch executable exists, so no GNU parity cases are claimed.
Real terminal input timing and fragmented multibyte delivery are deferred to a controlled private PTY fixture.
Nonseekable lookahead is owned by wget_wch; transparent mixing with Bash read or other raw FD consumers is not supported. Seekable file lookahead is rewound.

fstat identity distinguishes ordinary distinct anonymous pipes and descriptor switches. Reopened named FIFOs/TTYs with the same identity and recycled inode identities need a wider reader lifecycle/reset API; general reopen detection is not claimed.

The private pending-scalar cache has 1025 slots and does not evict saved lookahead. Closing an input before draining its pending scalar retains a slot for the shell lifetime. Exhaustion returns failure after the current cluster and lookahead were consumed; failure is not transactional.
Nonseekable lookahead is process-local: draining an owned stream across command substitutions or separate subshells is not supported. Tests keep successive reads in the same shell process.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports wget_wch as a builtin and help exposes its documented decode/read synopsis and output contract.
cases.script:
type -t wget_wch
doc=$(help wget_wch)
case $doc in *"wget_wch decode HEX..."*"read [FD]"*"Output is:"*) printf 'metadata-ok\n' ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac

cases.purpose: Check one-scalar output for ASCII with a following scalar, prefixed multi-argument hex, 3- and 4-byte encodings, and the highest Unicode scalar U+10FFFF.
cases.script:
wget_wch decode 4142
wget_wch decode 0xc3 0xA9
wget_wch decode e282ac
wget_wch decode f09f9880
wget_wch decode f48fbfbf
cases.stdout:
wch U+0041 bytes=1
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
wch U+20AC bytes=3
wch U+1F600 bytes=4
wch U+10FFFF bytes=4

cases.purpose: Check documented cluster extension handling for two combining marks, a variation selector, and an emoji skin-tone modifier; byte totals are summed from the supplied UTF-8 encodings.
cases.script:
wget_wch decode 61cc81e2839d
wget_wch decode e29880efb88f
wget_wch decode f09f918df09f8fbd
cases.stdout:
wch U+0061,U+0301,U+20DD bytes=6
wch U+2600,U+FE0F bytes=6
wch U+1F44D,U+1F3FD bytes=8

cases.purpose: Check that a ZWJ admits the following scalar and that a sequence can contain repeated joins; code points and byte totals are independently derived from the UTF-8 sequences.
Require rejection with diagnostics and no decoded stdout for odd/non-hex input, overlong and truncated UTF-8, a surrogate, an out-of-range scalar, and invalid read arguments.
cases.script:
rc=0; wget_wch decode 4 || rc=$?; printf "status=%s
" "$rc"; [[ $rc == 2 ]]
rc=0; wget_wch decode gg || rc=$?; printf "status=%s
" "$rc"; [[ $rc == 2 ]]
rc=0; wget_wch decode c0af || rc=$?; printf "status=%s
" "$rc"; [[ $rc == 2 ]]
rc=0; wget_wch decode e282 || rc=$?; printf "status=%s
" "$rc"; [[ $rc == 2 ]]
rc=0; wget_wch decode eda080 || rc=$?; printf "status=%s
" "$rc"; [[ $rc == 2 ]]
rc=0; wget_wch decode f4908080 || rc=$?; printf "status=%s
" "$rc"; [[ $rc == 2 ]]
rc=0; wget_wch read 3 extra || rc=$?; printf "status=%s
" "$rc"; [[ $rc == 2 ]]
cases.stdout:
status=2
status=2
status=2
status=2
status=2
status=2
status=2

cases.purpose: Read one UTF-8 scalar followed by a combining mark from a small pipe; expected code points and byte count come from the literal octal UTF-8 bytes.
Exercise the documented optional FD argument using a private here-string containing a three-byte UTF-8 scalar.
An empty input stream has no UTF-8 scalar to return and should fail without output or a diagnostic.
cases.script: rc=0; printf '' | wget_wch read || rc=$?; printf 'empty-status=%s\n' "$rc"; [[ $rc == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Two consecutive reads from the same descriptor must return the first two scalars separately; the documented operation reads one cluster, so boundary detection must not consume the next scalar.
cases.stdout:
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
wch U+0041 bytes=1

cases.purpose: Qualify terminal-facing read behavior when a multibyte scalar arrives in separate writes.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable private PTY plus a deterministic inter-byte input scheduler to distinguish a complete UTF-8 scalar from temporarily incomplete terminal input. The provided runner has no PTY driver; do not use a host terminal.

cases.purpose: A single wget_wch-owned anonymous pipe contains independently encoded combining and ZWJ clusters followed by ASCII; drain each cluster and confirm EOF.
cases.script: printf 'a\314\201\360\237\221\251\342\200\215\360\237\222\273Z' | { wget_wch read; wget_wch read; wget_wch read; if wget_wch read; then exit 91; fi; printf 'EOF\n'; }
cases.stdout:
wch U+0061,U+0301 bytes=3
wch U+1F469,U+200D,U+1F4BB bytes=11
wch U+005A bytes=1
EOF

cases.purpose: Two consecutive multibyte scalars must remain separate, followed by an ordinary ASCII scalar; byte counts and code points come from literal UTF-8 bytes.
cases.script: printf '\303\251\342\202\254Q' | { wget_wch read; wget_wch read; wget_wch read; }
cases.stdout:
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
wch U+20AC bytes=3
wch U+0051 bytes=1

cases.purpose: Alternate two owned input descriptors without moving pending scalar bytes from one stream into the other.
cases.script: { wget_wch read 3; wget_wch read 4; wget_wch read 3; wget_wch read 4; } 3<<<$'\303\251A' 4<<<$'\342\202\254B'
cases.stdout:
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
wch U+20AC bytes=3
wch U+0041 bytes=1
wch U+0042 bytes=1

cases.purpose: After caching lookahead from an owned pipe, duplicate it and redirect the original descriptor to a regular file. Each stream retains its own next scalar.
cases.script:
printf 'xY' > regular
{ wget_wch read 3; exec 4<&3; exec 3<regular; wget_wch read 3; wget_wch read 4; wget_wch read 3; } 3<<<$'\303\251A'
cases.stdout:
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
wch U+0078 bytes=1
wch U+0041 bytes=1
wch U+0059 bytes=1

cases.purpose: Independent here-strings reuse descriptor zero; old owned-pipe lookahead must not appear in the new pipe.
cases.stdout:
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
wch U+20AC bytes=3

cases.purpose: Regular file lookahead is rewound, so another reader sees the next byte and reopening the same file at offset zero returns its first scalar.
cases.script:
printf '\303\251A' > regular
exec 3<regular
wget_wch read 3
IFS= read -r -N 1 -u 3 next
printf 'next=%s\n' "$next"
exec 3<regular
wget_wch read 3
wget_wch read 3
cases.stdout:
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
next=A
wch U+00E9 bytes=2
wch U+0041 bytes=1
